title: Factual infographic: Planted Aquarium Nitrogen Cycle
tests: Explains the real planted-aquarium nitrogen cycle, bacterial conversion, plant uptake, testing, water changes, oxygen, and overfeeding risk without fictional claims.
prompt: Create a detailed factual infographic about the real-world nitrogen cycle in a planted freshwater aquarium, landscape educational poster style, clean modern science illustration. Show a cross-section aquarium scene with substrate, rooted aquatic plants, filter, fish, and water column. Use accurate conservative relationships, no fake exact numbers. Include a clear cycle diagram: fish waste and uneaten food produce AMMONIA, beneficial bacteria convert AMMONIA to NITRITE, other beneficial bacteria convert NITRITE to NITRATE, plants use NITRATE and AMMONIUM for growth, water changes remove excess NITRATE, filter media provides bacterial surface area. Include a small root-zone panel showing roots taking up nutrients from substrate/water. Include a simple warning panel: TEST WATER, AVOID OVERFEEDING, ADD PLANTS SLOWLY. Labels should be short and readable: AMMONIA, NITRITE, NITRATE, BENEFICIAL BACTERIA, PLANT UPTAKE, FILTER MEDIA, WATER CHANGE, ROOT ZONE. No fantasy, no fictional species, no fake exact ppm values, no brand names, no logos, no invented data. Visual style: crisp scientific diagram mixed with realistic aquarium textures, lush green plants, clear blue water, clean arrows, high readability, tasteful color palette of deep green, cyan, white, charcoal, and small amber highlights.

factualInfographic.description: A real-world aquarium-care infographic showing how waste becomes ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate, how nitrifying bacteria and plants interact, and why testing and water changes matter.
factualInfographic.sourceNote: Real-world/non-fiction topic; conservative aquarium-care basics, no invented statistics.
